terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation; with the accusative and infinitive, or dē with the ablative
evidence: Cic. Brut. 330: doleō mē in vītam paulō sērius tamquam in viam ingressum (Lewis & Short), s.v. sērus
Traupman p. 98: valdē dolēre dē (+ abl.)
terms.comment: Sorrow for what has happened, not an apology: mē paenitet is “I regret what I did”.

terms.gloss: heartache: tibi cordolium erit, you’ll be sorry
terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut.; in ōrātiōne solūtā rāra
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “sorrow at heart, grief (ante- and post-class.)”.

phrases.latin: Sī quid perperam fēcī, mē paenitet.
phrases.english: If I’ve done anything wrong, I’m sorry (an apology for a child)

sources: Lewis & Short: paeniteo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 112, 157, 383.
